fixes.explanation: Peter never says anything about asking elders in Joppa, a seaside city (Acts 10:5-6). He says God showed him that he should not call any man impure or unclean (Acts 10:28). Then he says, "So when I was invited, I came without objection." (Acts 10:29)

Priests aren't part of the reason Peter gives. He says Jesus went around doing good and healing all who were oppressed by the devil, because God was with Him. The reason he names is God being with Jesus (Acts 10:38).

Peter doesn't name the chief priests. He says Jesus was seen not by all the people, but by the witnesses God had chosen beforehand (Acts 10:41). Peter counts himself among those who ate and drank with Him after He rose from the dead.
There's no "only" in Peter's words. He says God appointed Jesus to judge the living and the dead (Acts 10:42). The Gentile nations aren't named in that sentence at all.
Peter doesn't limit it to Israel. He says Jesus is the One appointed by God to judge the living and the dead (Acts 10:42). Israel isn't named in that sentence at all.

No angel is mentioned in this scene. The ones astounded were the circumcised believers who had accompanied Peter. They were astounded that the gift of the Holy Spirit had been poured out even on the Gentiles (Acts 10:45).

The text doesn't mention a light. The ones astounded were the circumcised believers who had accompanied Peter. What astounded them was that the gift of the Holy Spirit had been poured out even on the Gentiles (Acts 10:45).

John, who proclaimed a baptism and baptized in the Jordan River (Mark 1:4-5), came up in Peter's sermon (Acts 10:37). But the baptisms in Cornelius's house were ordered in the name of Jesus Christ (Acts 10:48). John's name isn't the one Peter gave.

Abraham, the ancestor God promised to make into a great nation (Genesis 12:2), isn't named at all in this scene. Peter ordered them baptized in the name of Jesus Christ (Acts 10:48). That's the only name given for the baptisms.
The text never mentions synagogue elders. Verse 24 says Cornelius called together his relatives and close friends. That's a living room crowd, not a committee.

Right, Peter helped him up. He told Cornelius, "Stand up… I am only a man myself." (Acts 10:26) If somebody dropped down in front of me, I'd say the same thing, friend. I'm just a stamper with a big mustache.

The man in radiant clothing says, "Cornelius, your prayer has been heard, and your gifts to the poor have been remembered before God." (Acts 10:31) Both are named in that one sentence, prayer first and gifts second. Both are said to be before God.

That's not what Peter says. His opening line is that God does not show favoritism (Acts 10:34). Cornelius says a man in radiant clothing stood before him and told him, "…your prayer has been heard…" (Acts 10:30-31). Favoritism, not prophets, is what Peter names.

It's true. Peter says God welcomes those from every nation who fear Him and do what is right (Acts 10:35). Just before that, he told the people gathered that God had shown him he should not call any man impure or unclean (Acts 10:28).

Peter says Jesus went around doing good and healing all who were oppressed by the devil, "…because God was with Him." (Acts 10:38) That's the reason he gives for the doing good and the healing. He names God being with Him, and no other reason.

Not quite. Peter says Jesus was seen "…not by all the people, but by the witnesses God had chosen beforehand…" (Acts 10:41) So he doesn't say the crowds in Galilee saw Him. The ones who saw Him are the witnesses God had chosen beforehand.

Peter says, "…everyone who believes in Him receives forgiveness of sins through His name." (Acts 10:43) Everyone who believes, and it's through His name. Peter says it right after saying that all the prophets testify about Him.

Verse 44 says that while Peter was still speaking these words, "…the Holy Spirit fell upon all who heard his message." Not some of them, all who heard. The timing is right there in the verse: Peter was still speaking.

The text says the circumcised believers were astounded "…that the gift of the Holy Spirit had been poured out even on the Gentiles." (Acts 10:45) Gentiles are people who aren't Jews. I think the word "even" says a lot, because the gift reached people they weren't expecting it to reach.

Peter says the opposite. He says, "They have received the Holy Spirit just as we have!" (Acts 10:47) Just as we have, that's his comparison. He's measuring them against himself and the believers with him.
The text says, "Then they asked him to stay for a few days." (Acts 10:48) The verse tells us they asked, and it names a few days. I think that's a house that wasn't ready for the visit to end.
